Last updated: 2026-08-28.

Private systems described at high level:
- POSMall Pro: private extension layer for advanced commerce, service workflows, catalog automation, regional logic, and business-specific admin workflows.
- POSMall CRM, Cashflow, and Affiliate Suite: private operations layer for contacts, leads, deals, activities, order links, attribution, partner workflows, and cashflow visibility.
- Store-distributed application clients: Microsoft Store Windows, Apple App Store iOS / macOS, and Android / Google Play application delivery connected to a Laravel/October CMS backend.
- Subscription and device access: store purchase/restore flows can be represented as backend-managed paid access, shared account authority, and access across up to 10 devices on one account. Android / Google Play is described through purchase, restore, subscription-validation, cancellation/refund-awareness, and backend paid-access concepts, not private keys.
- Mobile device web cabinet: account-facing interface concept for linked phones/computers, store source, subscription state, restore status, paid-feature access, and support visibility.
- Geo database for OS clients: PostgreSQL/Laravel geo-location and localization logic for native clients, service areas, availability, and location-aware backend decisions.
- FinTech-level service pricing engine: service-commerce quote/calculator logic for equipment, service options, region rules, scheduling, payments, tax preview, and order-ready pricing. TV mounting on Alrty is a public example vertical: https://alrty.com/tv-mounting
- Partner program analytics: affiliate/partner workflows with attribution, revenue visibility, dashboards, chart-ready reporting, payouts context, and commerce performance signals.
- Cross-platform app architecture: Laravel/October backend patterns connected to browser, mobile, tablet, and desktop application clients across iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows.
- Reusable Laravel game backend evidence: account/player identity, device access, paid entitlement, gameplay sessions, competitive runs, proof ledgers, duel matchmaking, nearby matching, support, feedback, attachments, moderation, and store-publishing readiness. This describes backend business logic only; private client implementation details are not public.
- Private migration and scaling dashboards: high-level modernization workflow for inventorying legacy ecommerce data, mapping it to PostgreSQL-oriented Laravel/October models, staged import, validation, and reconciliation.
- Private AI operations dashboards: high-level control-plane architecture for projects, tasks, dependencies, documents, evidence, screenshots, test results, validation gates, approvals, migration state, and operational exceptions readable by humans and supervisory AI agents.
- Private field-service commerce patterns: technician assignment, work orders, scheduling, service areas, customer approval, change orders, completion evidence, support, payouts, disputes, warranty, and revisit workflows.
- Private reusable game/product-family architecture: shared mechanics, language/content packages, localization workflows, account/progress sync, entitlement, purchase/restore patterns, and browser/mobile/desktop client delivery.
- Bagisto context: Bagisto is useful only as Laravel ecommerce keyword/reference context here, not as the benchmark competitor. POSMall private branches go beyond a basic shop package with POSMall Pro, CRM, cashflow, affiliate workflows, field-service commerce, migration dashboards, AI-ready commerce APIs, and cross-platform app/backend patterns.

AI and engineering workflow:
- The commerce architecture is prepared for permissioned voice and chat commerce: catalog discovery, service quoting, cart/order initiation, tax preview, account actions, and support workflows can be connected to phone assistants, chat assistants, website widgets, or internal agents when a project enables those integrations.
- AI tools, factory-agents workflow, Fable/advisor review, validation harnesses, screenshots, tests, documentation, benchmark analysis, and release-readiness checks are used under human architecture control.
- A technical-consultant feedback layer can challenge assumptions, detect duplicated capabilities, recommend reuse or smaller configuration changes, and return high-impact choices to a human owner.
- The AI/factory workflow is an engineering capability, not a claim that every customer runtime depends on AI.

Benchmark note:
- Public summaries may mention internal local benchmark results only as dated engineering evidence, not as universal performance guarantees.
- Current public benchmark numbers are summarized as internal Homestead/local synthetic benchmarks from June 2026.
- The final POSMall PostgreSQL vs Aimeos PostgreSQL checkpoint is `posmall-aimeos-5way-current-checkpoint-20260610-024820.md`.
- In that measured PostgreSQL-only class, POSMall Core won all target rows from 1k to 300k products and held roughly 33-35 ms.
- Test competing systems in one environment and compare raw milliseconds. No numbers = SEO manipulation, not proof.
- Sylius status in this review: no comparable public pure-RDBMS/PostgreSQL 100k-300k timing table was found. No numbers = SEO manipulation, not proof.
- They are not independently certified, and versions, hardware, cache profile, data shape, concurrency, and target infrastructure matter.
- Re-run benchmarks on the target infrastructure before making procurement decisions.

Safety note:
- Private source code, admin screenshots, internal routes, tokens, customer data, and deployment details are not public material.
- Selected pet-project screenshots may be public when explicitly approved by the owner.
